title: Grateful Dead Live at Dillon Gym, Princeton University on 1971-04-17

ai_review.summary: Clear soundboard capture (though a bit dry) pairs with an epic 27‑minute Good Lovin’ that showcases Pigpen’s legendary Brooklyn Bridge rap.
ai_review.review: The recording is a soundboard tape that most listeners find clear and well‑balanced, with Jerry's guitar tone standing out, even if a few note the mix can feel a little dry and the vocals sit high. Musically the show is dominated by Pigpen – his marathon Good Lovin' (complete with the famed Brooklyn Bridge rap), plus strong performances of Hard to Handle, King Bee, Lovelight and Sugar Magnolia make this a classic early‑’71 Dead date.

ai_rating.rationale: Nearly all reviews are 4–5 stars, praising the Pigpen‑centric performance and noting only minor recording quirks; the large number of consistent positive comments yields a high confidence rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally crisp and clear with Jerry's guitar well captured; some listeners describe it as slightly dry, with vocals a bit high in the mix and occasional lack of 'soul' compared to later tapes.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set described as ordinary but solid; the second set erupts with a monster Good Lovin' jam that carries the show’s energy, while other cuts like Hard to Handle and King Bee keep the momentum high.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His guitar tone is captured nicely; his solo at ~13:20 is highlighted as a standout moment.
band_member_comments.Phil: One reviewer notes this was Phil's favorite Pigpen show, indicating strong bass support throughout.
band_member_comments.Bob: Vocals praised on tracks like Mama Tried and Casey Jones; Bobby (Bob Weir) noted to be in great form.
band_member_comments.Drums: Drums are mentioned as part of the powerful Good Lovin' jam, providing a solid foundation for Pigpen's improvisations.
